item.title: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker warns AI could extend lifespan or pose nuclear‑like threats
item.description:
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker warns AI could extend lifespan or pose nuclear‑like threats

Today I’m talking with Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker about his view of AI, tech and privacy.

🔍 Overview

Gov. Pritzker says AI is a technology that could help us live to 100 or threaten us like nukes. He is willing to discuss the “existential weeds” of what government is for when it comes to these sweeping possibilities.

🧩 AI & Society

  • Potential upside: Pritzker believes AI could extend human life to a century.
  • Potential danger: He warns AI could become a threat comparable to nuclear weapons.

⚙️ Government Role

  • Pritzker argues that many AI‑related challenges are collective‑action problems that require government intervention.
  • He stresses that we can’t solve these problems one at a time, or even one state at a time.

📊 Political Realignment

Pritzker notes a “big and maybe kind of unexpected political realignment” driven by three areas:

  • Data centers – a bipartisan backlash around their expansion.
  • Privacy – growing concerns across the political spectrum.
  • Antitrust – broader competition issues, especially in the AI industry.

🏛️ Antitrust & Competition

  • David Sacks retweeted Lina Khan (Biden administration) on whether the AI industry needs an antitrust exemption for safety.
  • Both agree AI companies do not need antitrust exemptions and should actually be more competitive.

📅 Why It Matters Now

  • The conversation comes as midterm elections approach, with early voting already underway.
  • Pritzker, a former tech‑industry businessman and self‑described progressive, says the stakes are “pretty high right now.”

The interview reflects a rare willingness from a governor to explore AI’s existential implications and the need for coordinated policy responses.

#AI #Privacy #Antitrust #Politics

Source: JB Pritzker on the good and bad of AI

item.title: Italy Antitrust Opens Probe into AI Music Startup Suno
item.description:
Italy Antitrust Opens Probe into AI Music Startup Suno

Italy’s antitrust authority announced on Tuesday that it has opened an investigation into Suno, an AI‑powered music‑generation startup, over concerns that some clauses in its terms of service may be unfair to consumers.

🔍 Overview

  • Investigation launched on Tuesday.
  • Targeted company: Suno, an AI music startup.
  • The focus is on potentially unfair clauses in Suno’s terms of service.

📣 Response

  • Suno was not immediately available for comment.

#AI #Antitrust #MusicTech

Source: Reuters Entertainment News Summary | International

item.title: Judge Dismisses Chegg and PMC Antitrust Lawsuits Over Google AI Search
item.description:
Judge Dismisses Chegg and PMC Antitrust Lawsuits Over Google AI Search

Federal Judge Amit Mehta dismissed the antitrust lawsuits brought by Chegg and Rolling Stone parent Penske Media Corporation, which alleged that Google’s AI‑powered search features siphoned traffic from their sites.

🔍 Overview

  • Chegg and PMC claimed Google abused monopoly power by coercing publishers into providing content for AI Overviews for free, or risk disappearing from search results.
  • The lawsuits, filed last year, asserted that Google’s AI search features diverted traffic away from publishers, hurting revenue.

⚖️ Legal Ruling

  • Judge Mehta wrote that the plaintiffs’ claims “don’t stand up to antitrust law.”
  • He noted the plaintiffs have only “pleaded an ‘expectation’ that Google will send them search traffic if they make their content available for free.”
  • “But an expectation is not an agreement. It is simply how a general search engine works,” Mehta wrote.
  • The court is “not ‘unsympathetic to the situation publishers now find themselves in,’” but said antitrust rules cannot replace legislative action on the economic impact of “new innovation.”

📉 Impact on Publishers

  • Publishers continue to see a steep dive in traffic to news outlets and small websites after Google’s AI‑powered search overhaul.

💰 Google Pilot Payments

  • This week, The Information reported that Google is paying around 100 publishers for their contributions to AI Overviews, AI Mode, and Gemini as part of a pilot program.

Disclosure: The Verge is part of Penske Media.

#Google #Antitrust #AIOverviews

Source: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
